0.content: Ei is Makoto's younger twin. Treasured Tales says Ei, a peerless warrior who thought she understood little of mortal hearts, gave up her body so Makoto could ascend; Makoto rebuilt it and made her a kagemusha (shadow warrior, body double). Together they were the one Raiden Shogun, light and shadow. Ei did the fighting so Makoto would not have to. Makoto's death in Khaenri'ah was, in Yae's words, Ei's greatest loss and the start of Ei's change.

1.comment: Makoto: Makoto's death in the cataclysm
1.content: When monsters overran Inazuma 500 years ago, Makoto went to Khaenri'ah alone without telling Ei, sensing the place could not be ignored. Ei followed, leaving the Kitsune Saiguu to defend Inazuma, but arrived only in time to hear Makoto's dying breath. Ei entered her unconscious sister's mind to say goodbye, cried bitterly and resolved to pursue Eternity. Ei saved Makoto's collapsing realm of consciousness and carried it back to Inazuma.

2.content: Musou Isshin was born from Makoto's divine might and named by her; she wanted it to witness "an Inazuma as lovely as a dream". Makoto was no fighter, so it was never sharpened while she held it; it stood for true peace. On the day she died it passed into Ei's hands, already stained with blood. Ei kept its name and has fought with it ever since.

3.content: The realm Ei rescued from Makoto's dying mind lies behind a torii gate in a cave beneath the Grand Narukami Shrine. Ei sealed it with her own hands. It resembles the Plane of Euthymia but differs in some way Yae cannot pin down. Yae calls it the foundation of the Sacred Sakura. In 2.5 the Shogun opened it so the two could duel at full strength; the duel lasted centuries inside and almost no time outside.

4.comment: Makoto: The Sacred Sakura and Makoto's seed
4.content: Makoto's lingering will gave Ei a seed of light: "the miracle tree that blesses the people". Ei planted it in Makoto's realm in the present, and it took root in Inazuma's past, growing into the Sacred Sakura that purified the cataclysm's filth and saved the nation. That is why everyone remembers the tree as ancient while Ei alone saw it appear after Makoto's death. Ei once failed to convince Yae of the link, because the seed had not yet been planted.

5.content: Both twins served Eternity, but differently. Ei sought stillness to resist erosion. Makoto cherished the present precisely because it passes ("If nothing else, we have the present moment," Ei recalls her saying) and held that dreams, the endless human drive to want a better future, are what is truly eternal. Ei calls Makoto's view simple on the surface but deeper and more far-sighted than hers. Accepting it ended the Sakoku Decree's logic.

6.comment: Makoto: Furuyama, the blind tea master
6.content: Furuyama served tea in the Raiden Shogun's retinue 500 years ago, nearly always to Makoto. Blind for years, he travelled Inazuma through Makoto's descriptions of her dreams. He repeated her creed that good things do not last, so one must enjoy life while it lasts and leave no regrets. When the cataclysm came he stayed behind as others fled, content. In 2.5 his memory leaked from the Sacred Sakura's roots, and he mistook Ei for the Shogun he knew. Ei brewed a final pot of tea in his memory.

7.comment: Makoto: The twins' circle of friends
7.content: In quieter times Makoto, Ei and their friends sat under the sakura trees playing karuta, with the Kitsune Saiguu offering prizes. Ei, always the most wooden player, pestered Makoto and Mikoshi Chiyo into practice matches until she finally won. Ei still remembers that tree and wishes time had stopped there.

8.content: In a cinematic of the limited 5.4 event Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival, Ei cuts through Mikoshi Chiyo's endless nightmare and takes her hand. Chiyo wakes in a dream picnic with Makoto, Ei, the Great Tengu Sasayuri and the Kitsune Saiguu. Ei tells her that only sweet dreams await her now, and in the present Ei sits alone as Chiyo's horn fades in her lap.

9.comment: Makoto: Makoto at the Mikawa Flower Festival
9.content: During the limited Akitsu Kimodameshi event (3.3), Ei told the Traveler that Makoto enjoyed the hagoita game Akitsu Hazura (Haneasobi) when the youkai's Hyakkiyakou still roamed Inazuma's nights. The twins attended the youkai's Mikawa Flower Festival once, and Makoto found it especially fascinating.

10.comment: Makoto: Baal and the two Raiden Shoguns
10.content: Yae Miko: "there were two twin gods, Baal and Beelzebul." Baal was Makoto. Because the twins ruled jointly, the world knew only one god, and both "Baal" and "Raiden Shogun" referred to both of them until Makoto died. Ei then took the Shogunate and kept the name. Few Inazumans know there was ever a change of Electro Archon; Ganyu hinted at it in Liyue, and Yae told the Traveler the full story in 2.1.
